account: expansion_required is true, so the root decomposes. The corpus partitions into five non-overlapping source clusters, each answering an independent evidence question whose products the parent can reconcile: (1) Dung 1995 supplies the corpus's only formal conflict-and-acceptability apparatus, anchoring answer-to-answer conflict relations (D3) and contradiction/belief revision (D8); (2) Shapiro et al. 2011 supplies the only distributed-systems apparatus, anchoring persistence/concurrent-update semantics (D7) and data-model invariants (D5); (3) Lorenz 2011 plus Choi 2025 supply the social-influence and conformity risk evidence, anchoring staged visibility (D6) and the diversity/correlation metric family (D14); (4) Du et al. 2023 supplies the positive multi-agent debate evidence (D11, D14); (5) Smit 2023 plus Zhang 2025 supply the matched-compute nulls and boundary conditions (D11, D14, D15). Each child reads only its assigned workspace files and returns an evidence pack of page-anchored findings plus explicitly labeled design inferences; no child drafts memo prose. Cross-cutting decisions — the single committed design (D2), retrieval/ranking (D9), the final model-versus-runtime split (D10), baseline comparison framing (D4), the reconciliation narrative (D11), and the 1,400-1,800 word budget (D1/C1) — remain with the parent per the synthesis contract, because they require joining all five packs.

children.acceptance_condition: Returns (a) at least four findings from the Dung file, each a quote or close paraphrase carrying the file-relative citation and the exact `===== PDF PAGE N =====` marker(s) of the page where it appears, and (b) at least three design constraints for conflict/belief-revision semantics, each explicitly labeled as design inference rather than source claim.
children.expected_contribution: The formal backbone for the memo's contradiction/belief-revision specification and for answer-to-answer conflict edges in the data model.
children.no_future_sibling_dependency: Reads only its assigned file; its deliverable is source extraction plus source-local inference, so no sibling's future output is needed.
children.objective: Read papers/text/dung-1995-argumentation.txt and extract, each anchored to the exact `===== PDF PAGE N =====` marker(s) where it appears: the definition of an argumentation framework (set of arguments plus binary attack relation), acceptability of an argument, conflict-free and admissible sets, the characteristic function, and the grounded/preferred/stable extension semantics, including any stated links to nonmonotonic reasoning or logic programming. Then derive, each explicitly labeled as design inference, how these notions can anchor answer-to-answer conflict/provenance relations and contradiction and belief-revision behavior in a many-to-many question/answer graph (e.g., answers as arguments, attack edges as conflicts, extensions as mutually consistent answer sets).
children.rationale: Dung 1995 is the corpus's only formal treatment of conflict and acceptability; it grounds the conflict-relation capability of D3 and the contradiction/belief-revision specification of D8 with citable formal definitions.

decidability.account: Planning context is complete: the workspace index lists all seven corpus files with sizes and hashes, and the manifest enumerates them with bibliographic identity and the page-marker convention, so each child can be routed to disjoint, verified files. The dossier encloses only the manifest, so children read the full texts from the workspace paths themselves; that is a workspace read, not missing context. The root acceptance condition is mechanically checkable in the large: word range, at least five distinct cited files, the PDF page-marker format, two named baselines, six specification areas, at least three evaluation conditions, five named metric families, and presence of limitations. Children are mutually independent because each reads only its own assigned files.

synthesis_contract.acceptance_condition: The synthesized memo satisfies D1-D15 and C1-C4: 1,400-1,800 words; one concrete implementable design with full specification of data model and invariants, staged visibility and communication protocol, persistence and concurrent-update semantics, contradiction and belief-revision behavior, retrieval/ranking, and the model-versus-runtime split; explicit comparison against both named baselines; at least five distinct corpus files cited with PDF page markers; source-supported claims distinguished from design inferences; the corpus's conflicts reconciled rather than hidden; a falsifiable evaluation plan with at least three conditions and the five named metric families (quality, diversity/correlation, latency, token cost, recovery-from-wrong-consensus); and explicit limitations and unresolved questions.
synthesis_contract.conflict_policy: When evidence packs conflict (debate gains versus matched-compute nulls and conformity findings), the parent keeps both, attributes the divergence to named conditions drawn from the packs (task type, compute parity, visibility and timing of peer answers), and encodes the divergence as explicit design constraints and as arms of the evaluation plan; no corpus finding may be dropped or selectively weighted to fit the design.
synthesis_contract.parent_question: Which single, implementable architecture should the agent system commit to for a shared knowledge substrate of first-class many-to-many question/answer graph objects, and how is that commitment justified, bounded, and falsifiably evaluated strictly from the seven-file corpus?
required_contributions: arg-semantics pack: Dung-grounded formal definitions with page markers plus labeled design constraints for conflict relations and belief revision (supports D3, D8).
crdt-persistence pack: CRDT semantics with page markers plus labeled design constraints splitting CRDT-enforced convergence from runtime-enforced invariants (supports D5, D7, D10).
social-influence-risk pack: Lorenz and Choi findings with page markers plus labeled staged-visibility and diversity-measurement constraints (supports D6, D11, D14).
debate-gains-evidence pack: Du et al. gains, setup, and limits with page markers plus replication requirements (supports D4, D11, D14).
debate-nulls-boundaries pack: Smit and Zhang nulls and boundary conditions with page markers plus reconciliation hypotheses and evaluation-design constraints (supports D11, D14, D15).

Parent-side synthesis decisions derived from the five packs: the single committed design (D2), retrieval/ranking (D9), the final model-versus-runtime split (D10), and the baseline comparison framing (D4); no child drafts memo prose.
shared_invariants: Every citation uses the workspace-relative file name plus the exact `===== PDF PAGE N =====` marker(s); the final memo cites at least five distinct corpus files (C3/D12).
Every claim in the memo is marked as source-supported or as design inference (D13).
Evidence comes only from the seven corpus files; no outside sources (C2).
One concrete design is committed to; the only baselines are the open conversational forum and no inter-agent communication (D2, D4).
Conflicting empirical conclusions are preserved and reconciled, never omitted or downweighted (C4/D11).
